From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 2,\,\,3-\frac{3z}{2}\le x\le 3,\,\,8-\frac{4x}{3}-2z\le y\le 4\}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $y,$ the $y$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(x)}^{{v}_{2}(x)}{\int }_{8-4x/3-2z}^{4}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/85d184f328ebdbed5faf2d1c43261940a8241b6637450ab5fe1c8d803026e273.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $xz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 2,\,\,3-\frac{3z}{2}\le x\le 3\}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom  boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(x),$ is 

$$
x=3-\frac{3z}{2}\,⟹\,z=2-\frac{2x}{3}
$$

and the top boundary of the region is

$$
z=2.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\,2-\frac{2x}{3}\le z\le 2\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/6ac58e4c98c79a1a698d052479b55a45dd2b79bed4ca11422d172fe306dac15f.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{2-2x/3}^{2}{\int }_{8-4/3x-2z}^{4}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x.
$$
